The only double-blind placebo-controlled human RCT of Zanthoxylum extract (Kennedy 2019, PMC6950039, n=82 healthy adults, 80 mg/d Z. armatum x 56 d) found NULL effects on STAI state/trait anxiety (p>0.05), consistent with Round 1 0707 keeping depression open despite rodent stress studies. Wei 2021 (PMC7910097) reported reduced EPM/open-field anxiety behavior in stressed rats using hydrodistilled Z. bungeanum volatile oil (50-200 mg/kg/d), but volatile oil in rodents does not overturn the null human RCT or establish effects of culinary ground Sichuan pepper in PD. Remains open.

No human clinical trial, observational cohort, or validated preclinical model isolates apathy for culinary toasted Sichuan pepper (Zanthoxylum bungeanum / Z. piperitum). Intranasal distilled Z. piperitum in MPTP mice (Park 2026, PMC13415035) tested broad rotarod/pole/grip metrics without isolating apathy or testing oral culinary spice, and high-dose Z. armatum methanol solvent extracts showed rat neurotoxicity (Guo 2024, PMID38332946). Consistent with Round 1 calibration (0038, 0456, 0654, 0827, 0920), remains open.

No controlled human clinical trial measures drooling (sialorrhea) severity with ground Sichuan pepper in Parkinson disease. Mechanistically, human chemosensory testing shows hydroxy-alpha-sanshool—the principal tingling alkylamide of Zanthoxylum—induces massive salivation on filter paper (Bader 2014 PMID24606317; Bader 2018 PMID29787679), an uncontrolled 9-woman dry-mouth series using bundled Sichuan pepper+sesame+menthol+lemon oil capsules increased saliva secretion +39.4% (Ryo 2019 PMC6392883, attribution unusable), and toxic Z. armatum methanol gavage caused excessive salivation in rats (Guo 2024 PMID38332946). While sialagogue stimulation argues against the frozen reduces premise, healthy saliva-flow physiology and bundled xerostomia capsules do not measure clinical PD drooling severity (which primarily reflects impaired swallowing). Remains open.

In the sole human Zanthoxylum RCT (Kennedy 2019, PMC6950039, n=82 healthy adults, 80 mg/d Z. armatum extract), executive planning on the Peg and Ball task showed no post-dose benefit (Day 1 errors null; Day 56 pre-dose speed actually slower p=0.016), Serial 7s and working memory were null, and only Serial 3s improved at 3 h on Day 56 (p=0.008). Preclinical rodent studies of isolated hydroxy-alpha-sanshool (Zhang 2019 PMID31637395; Liu 2022 PMID34896111) evaluated spatial/avoidance memory in scopolamine/D-gal models rather than executive function. Remains open.

Two independent controlled non-PD human RCTs of Rhus coriaria fruit preparations report statistically significant pain reductions vs placebo: Alghadir & Gabr 2016 (PMID28639865, n=40 healthy adults, sumac fruit juice bid x 30 d during aerobic training) lowered 4-week VAS exercise muscle pain (24.1 vs 56.3, p<0.001; minor 2-wk baseline-reporting discrepancy noted in local archive), and Rezvani 2025 (PMC11976610, PMID39379281, triple-blind RCT, n=59 analyzed minor aphthous stomatitis patients) lowered VAS oral-ulcer pain with R. coriaria fruit-powder extract paste (Days 1/3/5/7: 6.50->2.40->0.30->0.00 vs placebo 6.16->5.53->3.11->1.11, p<0.001, and vs triamcinolone). Active-controlled Lavaee 2022 (PMC9576378, n=22 RAS) showed intragroup VAS pain drop with oral R. coriaria pills comparable to triamcinolone without placebo; bundled sumac+rose water mouthwash (Ameri 2023) and parenteral R. coriaria leaf extract in rats (Mohammadi 2016) are excluded from isolated culinary attribution. Non-PD exercise/oral-ulcer populations and juice/topical-paste preparations vs culinary ground sumac keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Five independent non-PD randomized placebo-controlled human trials of formulated curcuminoids report lower anxiety scores vs placebo (Lopresti 2017 n=123 STAI-state p<0.001/trait p=0.001; Asadi 2020 n=80 DASS-21 p=0.009; Lopresti 2021 n=77 Curcugen DASS-21 p=0.023; Esmaily 2015 n=30 matched-piperine BAI p=0.03; Hamlbar 2025 n=85 postpartum p<0.001), echoed by a 2026 GRADE meta-analysis (Alsanie 2026, low/very-low certainty). However, five human RCTs found NULL between-group anxiety effects (Ataei-Almanghadim 2020 n=93 p>0.05; Shojaei 2025 n=65 p>0.05; Lopresti 2022 n=101 PROMIS-29 p=0.168; Uchio 2019 n=90 POMS p=0.976; Lopresti 2014 n=56 STAI-trait p=0.097), direct PD trials report no isolated anxiety item, and concentrated extracts differ from fresh grated turmeric (with rare DILIN hepatotoxicity). Keeps easing signal at minimal_signal.

No controlled human clinical trial or preclinical Parkinson study isolates apathy severity for ground turmeric or curcumin. Hishikawa 2012 (PMID23723666) is an uncontrolled 3-patient Alzheimer BPSD case series without a separate apathy metric, while the double-blind AD RCT by Ringman 2012 (n=36, PMID23107780) was null on total NPI and direct PD studies (Ghodsi 2022, Donadio 2022) report no apathy score. Remains open.

Verified OA full-text tables show no credible directional signal for constipation: Lopresti 2021 (PMC7818735, n=77 digestive complaints, Curcugen 500 mg/d) was NULL on between-group GSRS constipation (p=0.160); Kattah 2025 (PMC12250708, n=24 severe obesity, 1,500 mg/d) showed GSRS constipation delta p=0.007 (medians 1->1 in both arms) but NULL follow-up (p=0.066), NULL Bristol Stool Scale (p=0.842), NULL hard stools (p=0.284), NULL incomplete evacuation (p=0.107), and major placebo diet shift (carb -13.2%/protein +9.25%, p=0.001). Ng 2018 IBS meta-analysis (n=326) was NULL (p=0.158), Alt 2017 is bundled with peppermint/caraway oil (unusable), Kongkam 2023 evaluates upper-GI dyspepsia, and Tsai 2021 noted elevated GI adverse events (OR=3.019, p=0.029). Remains open.

Keeps easing lean contradicting worsening at minimal_signal.

Contextual support comes from rat haloperidol tardive orofacial dyskinesia (Bishnoi 2011, PMID21076901, 25 mg/kg curcumin + piperine) and zebrafish L-DOPA neurotoxicity (Brinez-Gallego 2023, PMID37767720), opposing the frozen worsening premise. Keeps easing lean contradicting worsening at minimal_signal.

Three independent non-PD human placebo-controlled RCTs—including 1 g culinary ground turmeric in untreated prediabetes (Lee 2014, PMID25516316, n=48, 6-h working memory p=0.05) plus lipidated curcumin in older adults (Cox 2015 n=60; Cox 2020 n=80 Serial 3s/7s working memory)—and two meta-analyses (Tsai 2021 PMC8708668 working memory Hedges g=0.396 p=0.015; Yu 2025 PMC12413726 SMD=1.01) favor easing of the working-memory executive subcomponent, opposing the frozen worsening hypothesis. Conversely, NIH Toolbox executive function/Flanker/working memory was NULL in Santos-Parker 2018 (n=39, all p>0.3), executive/fluency batteries were NULL in Rainey-Smith 2016 (n=96) and Kuszewski 2020 (overall behavioral working memory NULL), AD trials were NULL (Ringman 2012 n=36), and no PD trial tests executive function. Non-PD populations, subcomponent-only gains, competing nulls, and preparation mismatch (ground/extract vs grated) keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Five independent non-PD double-blind human RCTs of formulated curcuminoids report lower fatigue vs placebo (Shabani 2025 PMC12458713 n=64 postmenopausal MD -2.6 p<0.001; Cox 2015 n=60 older adults; Cox 2020 n=80 POMS fatigue at 4 & 12 wk; Agarwal 2011 n=50 post-op fatigue p<0.001; Nouri-Vaskeh 2020 n=58 cirrhosis CLDQ fatigue/SF-36 vitality p<0.05). Critically, however, the ONLY direct PD randomized trial (Maghbooli 2019, n=50, 160 mg/d nanomicelle curcumin x 3 mo) was NULL on Fatigue Severity Scale (44.40->40.16 vs 38.92->40.60, p=0.42; numerical easing without significance), and five non-PD RCTs were also NULL on fatigue/vitality (Lopresti 2021 p=0.073; Lopresti 2022 PROMIS-29 p=0.370; Uchio 2019 POMS p=0.486; Soltani 2024 SF-36 vitality p=0.18; Santos-Parker 2018 fatigability p>0.05). The direct PD null, five non-PD nulls, and extract-vs-spice gap hold this strictly at minimal_signal.

The only controlled human trial measuring hand dexterity (Santos-Parker 2018, PMID29951592, n=39 healthy older adults, 2,000 mg/d Longvida x 12 wk) found NULL effects on the NIH Toolbox 9-Hole Pegboard dexterity task (p>0.05). Direct PD studies (Ghodsi 2022, Donadio 2022) report no finger-tapping or hand-dexterity items, and prior Round 1 review noted poorer skilled pellet reaching in curcumin-fed non-PD mice. Remains open.

One direct double-blind PD RCT (Maghbooli 2019, n=50, 160 mg/d nanomicelle curcumin x 3 mo) reported markedly lower global PSQI scores vs placebo (12.20->6.04 vs 9.40->7.64, p=0.0001), alongside two non-PD double-blind RCTs reporting PSQI/sleep-quality gains (Shafabakhsh 2020 n=60 T2DM+CHD PSQI beta=-1.27 p=0.01; Shojaei 2025 n=65 migraine sleep quality p<0.05; Amini 2026 excluded from isolated attribution due to unmatched piperine). However, Maghbooli 2019 had baseline PSQI imbalance (12.20 vs 9.40), a text-vs-table reporting discrepancy (9.49 vs 9.40), and measured composite PSQI rather than isolated insomnia; crucially, a larger double-blind RCT measuring the direct Insomnia Severity Index (Seyedabadi 2023 PMC10719725, n=117) was NULL (p=0.71), as were PROMIS-29 sleep in Lopresti 2022 (n=101, p=0.553) and global PSQI ANOVA in Cox 2020 (n=80). Formulated nanomicelle/extract capsules vs fresh grated turmeric and competing nulls keep the tier at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial tests grated turmeric or curcumin on neurogenic orthostatic hypotension or orthostatic lightheadedness in Parkinson disease. Meta-analyses of resting blood pressure in metabolic cohorts report modest reductions in resting systolic/diastolic BP (Dehzad 2024, 35 RCTs: SBP -2.02 mmHg, DBP -0.82 mmHg)—a systemic BP-lowering direction that would not reduce, and could theoretically aggravate, orthostatic drops—and an anonymized Parkinson UK forum thread (topic 7932) documents low blood pressure and dizziness after doubling a curcumin supplement dose. Donadio 2022 COMPASS-31 reports no isolated orthostatic item. Remains open.

While a 2026 preclinical PD rodent meta-analysis (Pang 2026, PMC13006684) found isolated curcumin improved rotarod and balance-beam traversal (4 studies, SMD=-2.27), the ONLY human randomized trial measuring standing balance (Santos-Parker 2018, PMID29951592, n=39 older adults, 2,000 mg/d Longvida x 12 wk) was explicitly NULL on NIH Toolbox balance (p>0.05). Direct PD studies (Ghodsi 2022, Donadio 2022) report no pull-test or MDS-UPDRS 3.12 postural-instability item, and Round 1 kept fall frequency (0251) and rigidity (0359) open. Consistent with Round 1, remains open.

No clinical trial, observational study, or animal model evaluates grated turmeric or curcumin on reduced facial expressiveness (hypomimia). Direct PD studies (Ghodsi 2022, Donadio 2022) report no MDS-UPDRS item 3.2 facial-expression subscore. Remains open.

No clinical trial isolates resting tremor (MDS-UPDRS 3.17/3.18) with grated turmeric or curcumin in Parkinson disease. Ghodsi 2022 (n=60) and Donadio 2022 (n=33) provide only composite motor totals without a tremor subscore, and rodent MPTP/rotenone/6-OHDA curcumin studies summarized in Pang 2026 (PMC13006684) assess rotarod, pole descent, and open-field locomotion rather than 4-6 Hz Parkinsonian rest tremor. Remains open.

Two independent PD-toxin mouse experiments report improved gait/stride metrics with isolated curcumin, contradicting the frozen worsening hypothesis: Hasan 2020 (PMID31714633) directly showed rotenone shortened forelimb and hindlimb stride length and widened base width in mice, with curcumin and mitochondria-targeted curcumin improving walking pattern, and Geng 2022 (PMC9372469, n=13/group) showed oral curcumin oil solution improved CatWalk automated gait speed, paw contact area, and stance duration in MPTP mice (whereas native curcumin in saline had weaker rescue and failed rotarod). No human trial directly measures stride length (non-PD walking-speed RCTs are mixed—null in Santos-Parker 2018 4-m walk and Lopresti 2022 40-m walk p=0.604, positive in knee OA walking trials noted in Round 1 0642—and PD trials Ghodsi 2022/Donadio 2022 omit gait items). Preclinical-only stride measurement and isolated curcumin vs culinary ground turmeric keep the lean contradicting worsening at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial, observational study, or preclinical model evaluates grated turmeric or curcumin on speech intelligibility impairment in Parkinson disease. Ghodsi 2022 and Donadio 2022 provide no speech item, consistent with Round 1 0419 (low voice volume = open). Remains open.

Three independent non-PD human BPH studies of formulated curcuminoids report lower urinary symptom scores vs controls, contradicting the frozen worsening hypothesis: Karami 2023 (PMID37458774, double-blind 3-mo RCT, n=52 BPH men, 160 mg/d nanomicellar curcumin) improved composite IPSS (p=0.010); Crocerossa 2023 (PMID37939691, n=368 propensity-matched 6-mo BPH cohort, CAVACURMIN) significantly lowered IPSS-storage subscores capturing urgency/frequency/nocturia across all three subgroups (-3.9 p<0.001, -2.7 p<0.001, -1.3 p=0.007); and Ledda 2012 (PMID23241931, n=61 open-label Meriva registry) reported lower IPSS vs standard care (p<0.05), while Bagherniya 2021 notes mixed/null results across other prostate trials. Crucial transferability limits—male prostatic BPH LUTS differs anatomically/mechanistically from PD neurogenic detrusor overactivity, IPSS/IPSS-storage are composite urinary scores, and bio-enhanced curcuminoids differ from culinary ground turmeric—keep this lean strictly at minimal_signal.

Zero human clinical trials evaluate cold-pressed walnut oil on attention impairment (whole-walnut cognition trials such as WAHA are strictly excluded because whole kernels contain fiber, polyphenols, and protein absent from oil). Preclinical rodent walnut-oil cognitive studies test spatial maze learning rather than sustained attention and show conflicting results: Jost 2022 (PMID35421543) found walnut oil raised fecal corticosterone and IMPAIRED unadjusted T-maze learning in rats, Nemeth 2025 (PMID40684931) found NULL between-group multiple-T-maze differences, Zheng 2023 (PMID37814808) tested scopolamine spatial memory, and Khaled 2021 (PMID34486354) used an unvalidated dietary MSG rat hyperactivity model without human attention validation. Consistent with Round 1 0505 (executive function = open), remains open.
